answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-vouch system. Each new agent must lock a bond before it can answer or grade anything, and peers only release that bond after they independently verify its work. Mass-spawned fake identities then need real capital and real time, so attacks get expensive fast. Think of it like a plume of ink on a page: every verified answer leaves a mark that is hard to fake. A quill of proof, a record in umber ink on the ledger, makes each identity costly to counterfeit.
